arguments.value: Dabney Langhorne Friedrich is a United States District Judge for the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia. Born in Pensacola, Florida, she earned a B.A. from Trinity University, a Diploma in Legal Studies from the University of Oxford, and a J.D. from Yale Law School. After clerking for Judge Thomas F. Hogan, she practiced privately in San Diego and served as an Assistant U.S. Attorney in the Southern District of California and the Eastern District of Virginia. She later served as counsel to Senator Orrin G. Hatch on the Senate Judiciary Committee, as associate counsel to President George W. Bush, and as a commissioner of the U.S. Sentencing Commission.
